usageDetails.title: Checking Azure CLI release version information
usageDetails.explanation: Azure CLI uses Requests in a release-version lookup helper. It downloads a package's setup file from Microsoft's release storage, checks that the server returned a successful response, and reads the version declaration from the returned text. This lets the CLI obtain published version information without relying on a GitHub lookup in that code path.
flow: Build the release-storage URL for the selected Azure CLI package.
Fetch its setup file with Requests and check the HTTP response.
Read the version declaration and return the published version string.
usageDetails.scopeNote: This describes a specific Azure CLI version-check helper, not a measurement of Microsoft-wide usage or currently running downloads.

entries.summary: Meta's Python Business SDK declares Requests as an installation dependency.

usageDetails.title: Sending Graph API operations over HTTP
usageDetails.explanation: The SDK turns a Graph API operation into an HTTP request. It builds the versioned endpoint, adds standard headers, and places parameters in the query string for GET or DELETE, or in the body for other methods. A Requests session carries the call with uploads and timeout settings. The SDK then wraps the returned body, headers, and status in its own response object.
flow: The SDK builds the versioned Graph endpoint and request parameters.
Its Requests session sends the operation with headers and timeout.
The SDK wraps the response and raises any API error.
usageDetails.scopeNote: This describes the public Business SDK's Graph API transport. It establishes client functionality, without observing Meta's internal systems or live activity.

entries.summary: Google Auth includes an optional Requests-based transport for authenticated HTTP calls.

usageDetails.title: Adding Google credentials to HTTP calls
usageDetails.explanation: Google Auth offers an optional HTTP transport built on Requests. Its authorized session asks the credential object to prepare authentication headers, then sends the caller's HTTP request through the Requests session. If a response indicates that credentials need refreshing, the wrapper refreshes them and retries within its configured limits. Requests carries the network traffic while Google Auth manages credentials.
flow: Prepare authentication headers using the configured Google credential object.
Send the requested URL, method, and body through Requests.
Refresh credentials and retry when the response requires renewed authentication.
usageDetails.scopeNote: This is the optional Requests transport in Google Auth; other transports exist, and this is not Google-wide runtime telemetry.

entries.summary: The SageMaker Core package declares Requests as a runtime dependency.

usageDetails.title: Sending SageMaker SDK usage telemetry in background
usageDetails.explanation: SageMaker Core's telemetry helper records information about an SDK operation, such as its feature, outcome, environment and elapsed time. When telemetry is enabled, it builds a regional S3 telemetry URL and sends a GET request using Requests. The send runs in a background daemon thread with a short timeout, while request failures are handled without replacing the SDK operation's result.
flow: Check telemetry configuration and collect information about the SDK operation.
Build the regional telemetry URL with the collected event fields.
Send the GET request in a background thread with a timeout.
usageDetails.scopeNote: This describes SageMaker Core's configurable telemetry path, not every AWS API request or an independently observed customer deployment.

usageDetails.title: Fetching tokenizer data before local tokenization
usageDetails.explanation: tiktoken's data loader uses Requests when a tokenizer data location starts with HTTP or HTTPS. It retrieves the bytes and raises an error for an unsuccessful HTTP response. The surrounding cache loader can reuse a local copy, check an expected SHA-256 digest and save newly downloaded data, so a usable cached file avoids another download.
flow: Check whether the tokenizer data already exists in the local cache.
Fetch missing HTTP data with Requests and check the response status.
Verify the expected digest when supplied, then cache the downloaded bytes.
usageDetails.scopeNote: This covers tiktoken's public HTTP data-loading path, not OpenAI's API SDK or a claim about ChatGPT's internal traffic.

entries.summary: NeMo Speech's voice-agent service uses Requests to check a local model server's availability.

usageDetails.title: Checking an existing local model server
usageDetails.explanation: NeMo Speech's voice-agent integration checks whether a vLLM server is already listening on the requested local port. Requests calls the server's models endpoint with a five-second timeout. The helper reads the returned model identifier and can reuse the server when it matches the requested model, avoiding an unnecessary second server startup.

Request the models endpoint and read the returned model identifier.
Reuse the existing server when it serves the requested model.

Convert the downloaded media into image objects for the caller.

The returned hexadecimal data is converted back into bytes. This lets the tool exchange device commands through a configured proxy rather than a direct device connection.
